placement_finding.ncmoe_semantics_at_pin: whole-tensor: blocks < N experts CPU_Mapped (mmap-backed), blocks >= N experts get full VRAM buffers; verified by -ncmoe 16 OOM (136 GiB ROCm alloc attempt) and kv-4k verbose logs (CPU_Mapped 180.8 GiB, ROCm0 8.35 GiB)
placement_finding.model_vs_machine: model 186.0 GiB > RAM+VRAM 117 GiB; every viable run keeps nearly all experts mmap-paged — this is effectively the cold disk tier via page cache, validating the disk-tier thesis early
placement_finding.load_log_line: load_tensors: offloaded 47/47 layers to GPU (misleading; experts CPU_Mapped)

fa_decision.method: 256-token greedy gens at -ncmoe 45, seed 42 (ppl legs infeasible: prompt processing page-fault-bound at ~0.6 t/s -> one 2048-token window ~1 h; formal ppl gate deferred to M0.5)
fa_decision.coherence: both settings produce coherent, structured output with [Start thinking] delimiters
fa_decision.decision: fa = on (design decision rule 2); formal M0.5 gate owns the threshold

measurements.kv_detail: MLA: K-only f16, V=0; two buffers (n_embd 512 + 128); 77 MiB @4096 cells, 308 MiB @16384; plus fixed 145.56 MiB R/S decode state (ctx-independent)
measurements.vram_overhead_formula: peak - idle - ROCm0 model buffer (8550.87 MiB, from verbose log) - KV
measurements.cold_load_s: ~60 (first loads; later legs benefit from page cache)
measurements.copy_cost_ms_per_expert_layer_per_step: inconclusive: sweep N in {45,44,43} gave 0.8/0.7/0.6 t/s with INVERTED signal vs the copy model; page-cache noise (+-20%) dominates the ~5% expected copy signal. P4 per-step counters (M2.4) will measure this directly.

disk.io_uring: n/a (no fio on machine; deferred to M3 golem-store)
disk.note_t8_anomaly: 8-thread O_DIRECT legs DROP to 1.9-2.0 GiB/s on BOTH drives (vs t1) - concurrency regresses throughput; cause not investigated
disk.hardware_flag: RESOLVED (2026-09-20 follow-up): EIO is NOT a drive problem. Controlled matrix (5 legs/point): concurrent O_DIRECT reads on /home (btrfs, compress=zstd:3) fail EIO at t2=2/5, t4=5/5, t8=5/5, t16=5/5 legs; identical test on /mnt/data (ext4) 0 failures at every thread count; full single-thread O_DIRECT sweep of the 45.8 GiB shard = 5864/5864 chunks OK. Kernel/filesystem-level btrfs concurrent-O_DIRECT failure (kernel 7.1.11-arch1-1), no nvme errors in journal, PCIe AER clean, firmware 4B2QJXD7. M3.1 must probe O_DIRECT viability per replica at open and fall back to buffered reads (design §5.4 opt-in stance vindicated).

notes: warm_tok_s is NOT recorded as a number: at this pin there is no persistent device cache (P2/M2.4) and the sweep could not isolate copy cost; the extrapolation from §14 M0 is deferred to M2 hardware baselines.
